note: v1 (FIRST DRAFT): THE WARM THIRD. Relief, the first orbit closing, 136 bars (~300 s), 108 -> 112 bpm, flat across both 16-bar seams. LENS (1-16): t3's storm falls in holding D; t4 holds the residue of its D minor (add9) and at bar 9 the third LIFTS, F -> F#, as the first of E4's four lights (D9, cellos) takes over - D minor to D major is the relief. E4 'four lights' (this track's element: D9 / Bbmaj13#11 / Am11 / D9sus, one chord per E1 cycle, 20 beats a turn) is the clock from bar 17, its changes crossing the 4/4 bar lines. E1 (t1's seed, D A C G E) ASSEMBLES ITSELF on a handpan - one note more every two cycles - then answers itself in canon (kalimba, a fifth below, two beats behind) through B and the rise; the felt piano breaks E4 into eighths from 41; upright bass, a sine sub, a half-time brush groove and the chip's noise channel (nes-noise-hat, a 7-in-16 euclid: polymeter against 5 and 20) from 41 to 120. CREST at 81, where E1 (5), E4 (20) and the bar (4) meet one downbeat (beat 320 = 16 turns): a warm, close HUMAN VOICE (sung voice layer, humanize 0.5, larger tract, covered vowels, soft diction) sings four lines on E1 augmented then retrograded, coming home on D: 'around the warm stone / the cold half sleeping / I kept your far side / and turned toward you'; the last two lines return at 101. The fall (121-136) hands E1 augmented over the lights to t5. Mix: the first render was all low mids (spectrum 19: 213 Hz +17.6 dB, 14.8 kHz -26 dB, 38 Hz -22 dB), so cellos -6 dB at 220 Hz, bass -4 at 250, a sine sub under E4's roots, the chip air and a 6 kHz shelf: spectrum 19 -> 48. E2/E3 are carried only as the storm's residue so far (E2 not posted; E3 = t3's progression). NOT verified by ear.
